candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — coping mechanisms, anxiety reduction and therapeutic interventions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — coping with preoperative anxiety
candidate.educational_objective: Support client-selected, low-risk nonpharmacologic coping strategies for preoperative anxiety.

options.A: Choose a relaxation strategy that fits you, such as slow breathing or listening to preferred calming music, and practice it while waiting
options.B: Try not to ask any more questions because information generally worsens preoperative anxiety
options.C: Suppress signs of fear so the surgical team will not think you are too anxious for the procedure
options.D: Avoid all coping activities until after surgery because preoperative relaxation has no role in anxiety management

candidate.rationale: Nonpharmacologic coping strategies can be individualized to client preference. Relaxation techniques such as slow breathing and preferred music may reduce preoperative anxiety, while accurate information and supportive communication can reduce uncertainty. The nurse should not encourage suppression, avoidance, or discourage questions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Preoperative anxiety coping can include individualized relaxation, breathing, music and information/support.
candidate.source_document_title: Surgery: What can help relieve anxiety before surgery?
candidate.source_locator: Coping before surgery: people differ in coping; information/talking, relaxation such as slow/deep breathing, and music can help reduce anxiety
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
candidate.stem: A client awaiting elective surgery says, ‘I understand the procedure, but I still feel very tense and want something I can do myself to cope.’ Which nursing suggestion is most appropriate?
